differences.photo: Rock is broken into chunky plates with raised, rounded faces. Deep, dark, continuous cracks and ledges separate them, and each face has its own lighting and shading.
differences.generated: The surface is flat. The cell boundaries are thin, faint, wobbly lines, and the cells look like blurry colour patches rather than raised plates.
differences.fix: Raise the cell-border height contrast. Make the borders deeper and wider with dark, ragged crevices, and add per-cell height offsets and bevelled edges so the plates read as stepped blocks.

differences.photo: Pits are sparse and mostly small. A few are deep and dark, and the rest of the surface is smooth to mildly rough rock.
differences.generated: Thousands of small dark speckles and blobs cover the whole surface evenly. This looks like noisy confetti or terrazzo.
differences.fix: Cut the pit count by about 80%. Vary pit size more (a few large, deep pits and many tiny ones). Cluster the pits instead of spreading them uniformly, and make them lower contrast.

differences.photo: Saturated salmon and orange-pink, with bright pale highlights on the faces. There is grey-blue mottling in patches, dark orange-brown staining in the crevices, and small yellow-green lichen dots.
differences.generated: Washed-out, desaturated tan and beige with a hazy grey-brown overlay. Tonal range is low, with no strong highlights or deep darks.
differences.fix: Increase saturation and shift the hue toward pink-orange (about #d98a64). Widen the contrast, adding bright highlights on the cell tops and darker brown in the cracks, and use grey-blue as large soft patches.

differences.photo: Crisp, granular rock grain with sharp edges, small chips and pits, and visible directional lighting on the bumps.
differences.generated: Soft and blurry, with a smeared look. The detail is a uniform fine noise with no edge definition or directional shading.
differences.fix: Add a high-frequency grain or bump layer and sharpen the height map. Use a ridged or erosion-style noise at mid scale to give chipped edges.

differences.photo: Large, blocky, polygonal cells with angular corners and straight-ish edges. Cell sizes vary and there are overlapping ledges.
differences.generated: Large, round, organic blobs with smooth curved borders. They are too uniform and visually repetitive.
differences.fix: Use a Voronoi with a more angular metric and less domain warp, and vary cell sizes. Add a secondary set of small sub-cracks.

keep: Grey-blue patches in a few areas
